messages:
carmen: Heads-up — I'm trying to land a Terraform module + Helm values to make cluster-autoscaler behave better for our GPU node pools across AZs. Current problem: scale-down is evicting critical batch pods and we get uneven GPU capacity across zones. Anyone seen a good combo of TF + Helm config for this?

lee: a few quick wins: expander=least-waste, set balance-similar-node-groups=true, and bump scaleDownUnneededTime to something like 15m for long-running jobs. Also ensure PodPriority is set so important jobs are protected.

raj: adding: for preemptible/spot nodes we use taints + a "spot" node-group label. Cluster-autoscaler should skip nodes with local-storage if you have GPUs with local caches. In Helm values I add:
```yaml
extraArgs:
  expander: least-waste
  balance-similar-node-groups: "true"
  skip-nodes-with-local-storage: "false"  # we want it to consider these nodes unless pods use local storage
scaleDownUnneededTime: 15m
```

carmen: @raj re: taints — do you set eviction hard/soft thresholds somewhere? we're seeing pods get preempted before graceful checkpointing completes.

raj: we set pod disruption budgets + a custom pre-stop hook on training pods. For the autoscaler side, set scaleDownDelayAfterAdd to 10m and maxGracefulTerminationSec to 300 in the helm chart so nodes with GPU workloads get longer drain. Example TF snippet we use for node pool labels/taints: 
```hcl
module "gpu_nodepool" {
  source = "git::git@github.com:redwood/infra-mods.git//gke-nodepool"
  name   = "gpu-${var.zone}"
  labels = { "redwood.workload" = "gpu", "spot" = var.use_spot ? "true" : "false" }
  taints = [{ key = "nvidia.com/gpu", value = "present", effect = "NoSchedule" }]
}
```

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered: terraform plan for module gpu_nodepool (PR #421) — started by carmen.

ops-sre: cost note — if you force balancing across AZs you might pay a bit more in minimum reserved GPUs. Could try a staged rollout: start with expander=least-waste + scaleDownUnneededTime, monitor 24-48h, then enable balance-similar-node-groups. Also watch for IP exhaustion in smaller subnets when autoscaler brings many nodes up.

lee: +1 on subnet/IP checks. If we need more headroom, bump cluster-pod-cidr per AZ or enable secondary IP ranges for nodes in the TF module.

carmen: perfect, thanks. I'll open a PR with: TF nodepool labels/taints, helm values like you suggested (expander, balance-similar-node-groups, scaleDownUnneededTime=15m, scaleDownDelayAfterAdd=10m, maxGracefulTerminationSec=300), and a note to monitor IP usage and cost. Assigning to @lee for review. :raised_hands:

lee: cool — ping me when PR is ready and include a short playbook for rollbacks if scale-down still misbehaves.
